title: at a string hint whose toString returns an object the walk continues to valueOf, so a capability-reading valueOf is charged at a string position after all
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Inference': 'Requirement inference MUST be transitive through ordinary calls.' Which member a coercion calls is decided by ECMAScript's `OrdinaryToPrimitive`, and this case is the half of that algorithm a compiler is most likely to flatten away. With a string hint the walk tries `toString` first; here `toString` returns an OBJECT, which is not a primitive, so the algorithm does not stop — it goes on to `valueOf`, which reads Db. The row is therefore charged at a position that looks purely stringy. WHY THIS CASE AND ITS NEGATIVE SIBLING MUST BOTH EXIST: `coercion-members-that-never-run-charge-nothing` pins the ordinary string-hint case, where a Db-reading `valueOf` is NOT charged because `toString` returned a primitive first. Read alone, that case invites the simplification 'a string position never charges valueOf', and this case is the program that simplification gets wrong. Read alone, this case invites the opposite simplification 'a string position charges everything', and the negative sibling is the program THAT gets wrong. Neither statement is safe without the other, and the pair is what makes the walk itself the contract rather than a lookup table of positions. Both member spellings are declared — a method shorthand and an arrow property — because the fall-through has to survive the spelling axis too: a backend that reads the walk correctly for prototype methods and loses the arrow-valued one answers this case with one diagnostic instead of two. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: the run-time outcome. Coercing an object whose `toString` and `valueOf` both refuse to produce a primitive is a TypeError in ECMAScript, and this program never reaches run time on either backend because it is refused; declaring an `output` expectation here would be pinning the host's error, not the language's rule. It also does not pin the diagnostics' order, which the judge compares as a sorted multiset. `messageContains` is declared once and holds both to Db, because two refusals at two positions are satisfied by code and position alone whatever the row named; the bare capability name is the fragment that works on both backends, which render a row as `Db` and `{Db}`. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the SECOND declared line from 26 to 25 — collapsing the two onto one position, which is what a backend that saw the first spelling twice would report — turns the case red on BOTH backends with the position diff printed, and the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 b17b71eea3ea07f7e3383532805cf8688bb175f08de3efcf1b17b71bae26dab6 before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently).
